newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO KEEP EYES ON FRENCH TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO KEEP EYES ON FRENCH TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: Monaco are determined not to let thoughts of Newcastle cloud their vision as they try to put their French first division title challenge on course again when they travel to Rennes on Thursday.
"If we want to be champions, which is our chief objective, we must win there (at Rennes), it's imperative," Brazilian striker Anderson said.

Midfielder Ali Benarbia said: "Every match is important for us now and we must not lose those to come. We know that a victory for three points can quickly change things...and we must work on that basis."

Monaco's advantage over second-placed Paris St Germain was cut to four points on Sunday when the leaders were held 0-0 at home by defending champions Auxerre, their second league match without scoring.

The Rennes match has been brought forward from Friday to give Monaco another day's preparation for the second leg of their UEFA quarter-final at home to Newcastle United next Tuesday. They won the away leg 1-0 through an Anderson goal.
Anderson must, however, rediscover his domestic finishing after going two league games without scoring after a prolific spell of six goals in five successive games.
The Brazilian is not the only striker to have gone off the boil lately.

Stephane Guivarc'h, whose 17 goals helped Rennes build a home record better than all bar Monaco's in the first division, has not found the net in five league games this year after a hat-trick against Marseille on December 20.

Rennes, who have scored only one goal this year, lost their 12-game unbeaten home run to Nantes in their last home match last month and Strasbourg's David Zitelli has overtaken Guivarc'h as top marksman.
But Monaco coach Jean Tigana warned: "We know we have a very tough match ahead of us against a team which will have no complexes about us and Rennes are very effective at home.
"They have one of the best attackers of the championship in Guivarc'h who we're going to have to watch very closely."
Monaco will be weakened in defence by the absence of French international goalkeeper Fabien Barthez and defender Patrick Blondeau, who is ill.

Barthez, who will be replaced by Stephane Porrato, had an operation on Monday on a broken cheek bone suffered in the Newcastle match and is being given time to recover for the second leg against the English side. He faced Auxerre with a protective bandage.
Teenage striker Thierry Henry, who turned out for France's under-21 side on Wednesday, is also unlikely to play.
Benarbia added his own warning: "The first danger is ourselves, we know that and we've often said so.

"We must worry above all about playing our own game, that's how we resolve all manner of traps tended by our opponents. The most important thing is that we have not lost our spirit of combativity and sacrifice."
